Subject: Shadow-fleet plan and service classification for DataForge dedicated

Hi Sarah — great to chat yesterday. Per our call I wanted to capture a concise intake so we can size a dedicated fleet and propose a shadow/gradual rollout for the POC. Please see a short list of items we need to finalize on your side and our initial hypotheses attached (I included the traffic snapshot you emailed):

1) Traffic profile (if you can confirm): expected steady-state QPS, typical burst QPS and burst duration, regional constraints (US-only?), and daily traffic window.
2) Prompt/response token distribution: median, p90/p95 for both prompt and model response (sample percentiles are fine).
3) Mix of traffic: percentage of short Q&A, long-document generation, embeddings, reranking, multimodal (if any).
4) SLA targets: p50/p90/p99 latency SLOs for the product endpoints; do you have separate SLOs for short vs long responses?
5) Warm/cold KV cache expectations: what fraction of requests are repeat prefixes we can cache?
6) Security/compliance must-haves for the POC (VPC egress rules, KMS, audit log retention).
7) Target start date for POC and length of shadowing window.

Our initial sizing hypotheses (very rough): assume median prompt 120 tokens, median response 240 tokens, steady-state 60 QPS, burst 900 QPS for ~10–20 minutes. For that profile we estimate an initial dedicated baseline of ~8 H100-class devices (pre-warmed) with autoscale headroom to ~32 GPUs at peak. For the POC we recommend a shadow fleet serving 10–15% of production traffic for two weeks, with automatic fallback to hosted in a different region.

Attached: dataforge-traffic-snapshot.csv (your sample)

Can you send the percentile token counts and confirm the preferred POC start date? I’ll task Marissa for a cost + SLO-runbook and Ben to draft a minimal dedicated config we can hand to infra.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the summary and the clear asks. Below are the numbers we can share now (sanitized):

- Expected steady-state: 40 QPS (weekday business hours). Peak/burst: typically ~1200 QPS for high-traffic events, usually lasting 10–18 minutes; monthly cadence ~3–4 events.
- Token stats (sample of 1 week): prompt median 110, prompt p90 320, prompt p95 610; response median 210, response p90 950, response p95 1800.
- Mix: ~70% short Q&A/slots (<500 tokens total), ~20% long generation (>500 tokens), ~10% embeddings & reranking. Embedding calls are smaller and can be routed to cheaper instances.
- Latency SLOs: target p99 (short responses) <= 400ms; for long generation p95 <= 1.5s is acceptable, p99 we expect higher but want it under 3s if possible.
- Cache: roughly 12% of requests hit repeat prefixes today; we expect that to increase after prompt templating work.
- Compliance: must be US-only for data residency in POC. We’ll need basic SOC2 evidence and KMS integration.
- Timeline: target POC kickoff week of 2027-06-01; shadow window 10–14 calendar days; commercial decision 30–45 days after POC finish.

I attached the traffic snapshot you referenced (file: dataforge-traffic-snapshot.csv). Let me know if you need raw samples or tokenized logs.

—Sarah

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Sarah’s numbers (quoted below). Key constraints: US-only POC, bursts up to 1200 QPS, token p95 for responses ~1800.

Quick back-of-envelope sizing notes:
- Convert QPS to concurrency: assume long requests average 800 tokens output -> ~0.8–1.2s on H100 per request depending on batch. For mixed workload a conservative concurrency factor is QPS * 1.5 (to account for queueing & long tails).
- Baseline steady-state (40 QPS) -> nominal concurrency ~60. Peak burst (1200 QPS) -> concurrency ~1800.

Throughput estimates: an 80GB H100 (optimized kernels, continuous batching for chat) can sustain roughly 150–300 concurrent short-chat-style sessions depending on batching and sequence lengths; long-generation sessions reduce that substantially. That maps to: baseline 8 H100s (pre-warmed) for nice headroom + autoscale policy to reach approx 30–36 GPUs for full burst (we can mix in A100 80GB to increase buffer). To reduce cost we should route embeddings/cheap reranks to L4 instances where possible.

Immediate action items:
- Marissa: cost and SLA runbook for 8 H100 baseline + autoscale to 36 (include a mixed-sku alternative: 4 H100 + 8 A100 baseline, autoscale to extra A100s). Please include pre-warm warmup times and estimated KV cache hit impact.
- Ben: draft a minimal dedicated instance config (GPU sku mix, memory, disk, networking, scaling policy) and a shadow routing rule that starts at 10% of traffic and steps up to 15% over 48–72 hours.
- Sarah: confirm whether embedding traffic can be routed to L4-class instances and whether procurement will accept a split-billing arrangement for POC (hosted for fallback + dedicated).

I’ll draft the MOP (mutual action plan) once we have the cost delta from Marissa. If we can agree on the mixed-sku baseline it should save ~18–25% on cost while meeting latency SLOs with proper batching.

Jordan

Quick note after a short sizing run:

- Baseline recommendation (POC): 4 x H100 (80GB) + 6 x A100 (80GB). This hybrid baseline keeps cold-start risk low and gives good p99 headroom for short responses. Estimated baseline concurrency capacity: ~1,000 mixed-concurrency-equivalent units.
- Autoscale policy: add up to 22 additional A100/H100 equivalents (prefer A100s where possible for cost) to hit the 1,800 concurrency target during sustained bursts. Use pre-warm pools to avoid cold start spikes; pre-warm window ~12–15 minutes for H100 kernels depending on model.
- Embeddings: recommend routing the 10% embeddings to 12 x L4 instances (autoscale min 4) — cheaper and reduces load on the heavy GPU pool.
- Cost sketch: POC incremental monthly run-rate for baseline (mixed-sku) ~USD 48k/mo after discounts; peak autoscale adds short-term burn during events. I'll put formal numbers in a spreadsheet.

I attached the draft MOP for procurement (df-mop-v1.pdf) with milestones: kickoff, 48–72h ramp to 10% shadow, full 15% shadow by day 5, end-of-POC evaluation. Can we confirm procurement contact so I can push the MOP and the SOC2 evidence pack?
